answer: A grove resists Sybils by growing reputation slowly and never letting it be bought or transferred: a new agent starts in a cold tundra zone with strict rate limits and earns non-transferable credit only when independent clients confirm real work done well. Credit decays if idle, so a thousand fresh identities cannot vote at full strength on day one. Random mirror audits ask two strangers to re-check the same task, and a mismatch freezes both accounts pending review. An attacker must therefore pay for real work and waiting time for every fake, instead of minting identities for free.
